text:
priya: heads-up — i'm about to push the tf module refactor for our iam and kms wiring. main change is splitting aws-provider usage into a root provider + per-module aliased providers. goal: make future module upgrades less risky. quick Q: should we update the providers.lock at the repo root before or after the module split?

 dave: i'd prefer before — run `terraform init -upgrade` and commit the lockfile so CI validates module consumers. otherwise people will get varying provider versions when they run init locally. :+1:


jen: small wrinkle: the refactor changes module source paths and moves kms secrets into a new module. CI's plan job currently runs `terraform init` in the module directories, not the repo root. if you update the root lockfile we need to ensure module-level inits don't override it. i'd add a check in CI: `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=darwin_amd64` and commit the generated `.terraform.lock.hcl` next to the root `versions.tf`.


priya: ok that makes sense. so workflow: 1) push refactor branch (no lock changes), 2) run lock generation locally from root, 3) update CI to validate lockfile and prevent module-level `init -upgrade` in PRs. anyone object?


jen: also echo on pinning provider constraints. recommend we keep `required_providers` ranges narrow-ish, e.g.:

```
terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 4.60"
    }
  }
}
```

that avoids surprise minor bumps while still allowing patches. mention it in the PR description.


priya: thanks. dave — can you share the quick command you use to regenerate the lockfile? i'll include it in the dev guide snippet.


 dave: sure — from repo root i do: `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR=.terraform/plugins terraform init -input=false -upgrade` then `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=darwin_amd64`. then commit `.terraform.lock.hcl`.


priya: perfect. evan — can you run the staging plan once i push? just want a sanity check on state moves and provider aliases. no prod apply without a green smoke test.


 evan: yep i'll kick off after your PR lands. i'll also add a short test that applies to a throwaway workspace using the aliased provider to ensure resource address stability.


infra-bot: deploy-checker: new PR created for branch `priya/tf-module-split-kms`. CI status: pending — plan job queued.


priya: cool. i'll update the PR with the lockfile and the description steps. tagging @dave @jen for review and @evan for staging plan once it's green. ty!


jen: one last note — add a blurb in the changelog about the provider aliasing pattern so future contributors know why it's structured this way. small docs save a lot of time. :memo:


priya: will do.
